Dublin's bike-share network shrank sharply in early 2018, with total docking capacity falling 23% in one month

Why this matters

The sharp drop in docking capacity occurred during a period of transition in Dublin's bike-share landscape. In mid-2018, stationless operators were licensed to complement the existing Dublinbikes scheme, and the scheme has faced ongoing challenges with network expansion. Understanding these capacity fluctuations is important for assessing the reliability and coverage of shared cycling infrastructure as the city seeks to expand sustainable transport options.

Related: Breaking: Bleeperbike and Urbo get licences to run stationless bicycle share in Dublin City – IrishCycle.com
  • Between early January and early February 2018, the average number of bike stands per station dropped from 31.95 to 24.54, a 23% decline that marked the sharpest period-over-period change in the dataset
  • Across all records, open stations accounted for 597,838 total bike stands, dwarfing the 5,520 stands at closed stations by 99% — though only 0.7% of station records (138 of 20,000) showed a closed status
  • Available bike stands and available bikes showed a moderate negative correlation of -0.716, reflecting the expected trade-off: when more bikes are docked, fewer stands are free
A caveat worth knowing: This sample covers just one month (January 8 to February 8, 2018) and does not reflect current network capacity or seasonal patterns across the year
